---
title: "check-heading-titles.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that flags a clickbait heading.
It fails by default, since agents ignore warnings (Ezra, 2026-11-02).
A heading is a plain noun phrase that names its content (Ezra, 2026-11-03):
it is not a question, and neither it nor a phrase after a colon
begins with who, whom, whose, what, when, where, why, how or which.
The rule text is in psw, "Subsection headings".

The check reports two mistakes:

- **Question.**
  The heading text ends with `?`.
- **Interrogative start.**
  The heading, or any phrase after a colon in it, begins with
  who, whom, whose, what, when, where, why, how or which.
  A word that only begins with one of these,
  such as "Whatever" or "Howell's", does not count.

The check also reads the title of a fenced div or callout:
the `####` heading inside a definition, example or exercise div,
or a `title="..."` attribute on the div's opening fence.

The check does not count:

- a heading inside a code fence, an HTML comment or the YAML front matter;
- a heading on a line carrying `<!-- check-heading-titles: allow -->`.

## Scope

A finding is reported only when the heading line was added in the pull request,
so existing headings are not swept.
With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed,
the check skips with a warning instead of scanning the whole tree.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked page in full on purpose,
which measures how many headings a corpus carries that break the rule.

## Inputs

| Input          | Type    | Default    | Description |
| -------------- | ------- | ---------- | ----------- |
| `globs`        | string  | `'*.qmd'`  | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore` | string  | `''`       | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`         | boolean | `true`     | Fail the workflow when an added heading is clickbait. Set `false` for warning annotations only. |
| `whole-tree`   | boolean | `false`    | Scan every tracked page in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string | `'3.x'`   | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-heading-titles.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags a clickbait heading when a PR adds it: a question, or a
# heading (or a phrase after a colon) that starts with who, whom, whose, what, when,
# where, why, how or which.
# Fails by default.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check heading titles

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-heading-titles.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd'                         # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'   # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: false                            # warn instead of block (defaults to true)
    #   whole-tree: true                       # scan every page, not just a PR's additions
```

See
[`examples/check-heading-titles.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-heading-titles.yml)
for the full caller stub.
